chapter_summary: Proverbs 25 is a collection of wisdom sayings copied by the men of King Hezekiah. The chapter moves through royal wisdom, relational wisdom, and the wisdom of self-control. It teaches that God keeps some things hidden, that kings are meant to search out truth, and that wise speech — kind, timely, and restrained — has tremendous power. The chapter also calls God's people to unexpected acts of kindness toward enemies, to patience in persuasion, and to the vital discipline of governing one's own spirit. The final image of a city with broken walls is a warning: a person without self-control is wide open to every danger.
main_lesson: Wise words spoken at the right time are like precious gold. And the person who controls themselves is stronger than any warrior.

memory_verse.kjv: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
memory_verse.little_bible: The right word said at the right time is precious. It is like golden apples in a silver frame.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 25 opens with a profound theological observation: God conceals things, and it is the glory of kings to search them out. This tension — between divine hiddenness and human inquiry — sets the tone for the whole chapter. Wisdom is not passive; it searches. It examines. It does not presume to know what God has hidden, but it diligently seeks what God has revealed. For your children, this is an early lesson in intellectual humility and earnest seeking.

The middle section of the chapter deals with speech and relationships. The famous 'apples of gold' image (v. 11) is perhaps the most memorable picture of timely wisdom in all of Proverbs. Words are not all created equal: the right word, in the right moment, in the right spirit, is extraordinarily beautiful and valuable. Help your child understand that learning when to speak, how to speak, and what to say is a lifelong craft — and one God calls us to pursue.

The chapter also contains a striking command: feed your enemy when he is hungry, give him water when he is thirsty (vv. 21–22). This is not soft moralism — it is radical counter-cultural love, grounded in trust that God will sort out justice. Jesus extends this principle in the Sermon on the Mount. This is a wonderful place to help children see that the Old Testament was already calling people to love their enemies.

The closing verse about the city without walls is the chapter's urgent warning. Self-control is not just a personal virtue — it is structural protection. A person with no rule over their spirit is as exposed as a city with no walls. Help your children see that the daily discipline of self-control — in anger, in appetite, in words — is itself an act of wisdom and safety.
application_for_children: This week, practise saying the right thing at the right time. Before you speak, ask: 'Is this true? Is this kind? Is this the right moment?' That is what golden words look like.

verses.kjv: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
verses.little_bible: These are more wise sayings from King Solomon. Men who worked for King Hezekiah carefully wrote them down.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: King Solomon's wisdom was carefully copied and saved.
verses.meaning: This verse is a historical note establishing the provenance of Proverbs 25–29. King Hezekiah (a godly king of Judah) had scribes who preserved Solomon's wisdom. Wisdom is worth preserving — it doesn't just happen; people work to pass it on.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for people who save Your wisdom.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to write down and save wisdom?
verses.family_discussion: How do we pass wisdom down in our family — not just by example but by actively teaching and recording it for the next generation?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one piece of wisdom you have received from a parent or grandparent. Keep it somewhere safe.
verses.illustration_prompt: A scribe carefully copying glowing words from a scroll by candlelight, ancient setting, warm golden watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.
verses.little_bible: God is great, and He keeps some things hidden. But wise rulers search out the truth in every matter.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God hides things. Wise leaders search them out.
verses.meaning: God's concealment is not deception — it reflects His infinite depth and sovereignty. For human rulers and seekers, the honour lies in diligent inquiry. God invites us to search; He does not reveal everything at once, but He rewards earnest seeking (see Proverbs 2:4–5).
verses.prayer: God, help me search for truth and wisdom all my life.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think God hides some things for us to find?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children intellectual humility — knowing what God has not revealed — alongside the courage to search diligently for what He has?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a big question about God or life today. Spend time searching for an answer in the Bible or with a parent.
verses.illustration_prompt: A glowing hidden treasure behind a curtain, a curious child on one side reaching toward it, wonder and light in the scene, watercolour style

verses.kjv: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, so the heart of kings is unsearchable.
verses.little_bible: The sky is too high to measure. The earth is too deep to reach the bottom. A king's heart and mind can be just as hard to fully know.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Like the sky above, a king's heart runs deep.
verses.meaning: Great leaders have depths of thought and motive that are not easily read. This is not a warning against kings but an observation about the complexity of great minds — wisdom operates at depth, not on the surface.
verses.prayer: God, give me a heart that goes deep with wisdom.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean for something to be too deep to fully know?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a respect for depth — in God's Word, in people, and in wisdom — rather than assuming they can understand everything quickly?
verses.do_it_today: Look up at the sky today and think: 'God's wisdom is even higher than that.' Let it fill you with wonder.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child looking up at an infinite sky and then down into a deep well, both endless and vast, warm watercolour scene with wonder

verses.kjv: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
verses.little_bible: When you remove the bad parts from silver, something beautiful and useful comes out. The pure silver becomes a fine and lovely vessel.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Remove what is bad and something good emerges.
verses.meaning: Dross is the impurity that appears in silver when it is heated. Removing dross is what allows beauty and usefulness to emerge. This is a picture of purification — the process of removing what corrupts so that the true, valuable thing can shine.
verses.memory_phrase: Remove the bad. See the good.
verses.prayer: God, take away what is bad in me. Make me something beautiful.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you clean something that was very dirty or impure?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children welcome the refining process — correction, discipline, growth — as the way to something beautiful?
verses.do_it_today: Find something in your room that needs cleaning. Clean it. Think about how God cleans us from the inside.
verses.illustration_prompt: A silversmith melting silver, impurities rising away, a pure shining vessel emerging from the process, warm firelight and wonder, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Take away the wicked from before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
verses.little_bible: A king who removes wicked people from his court builds his throne on what is right. Righteousness makes a leader's rule strong and lasting.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Remove the wicked. Build a throne of righteousness.
verses.meaning: A ruler is only as good as those who surround and influence him. Wicked counsellors corrupt leadership. Removing wicked influence is not just political strategy — it is the foundation of just government. This principle extends to every sphere of influence in life.
verses.prayer: God, help leaders around me choose what is right.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it matter who a leader listens to and spends time with?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that who they surround themselves with shapes who they become — and that godly community is not optional but essential?
verses.do_it_today: Think about your closest friends. Are they making you wiser and more righteous? Thank God for the good ones.
verses.illustration_prompt: A king on a throne, a wise counsellor beside him and dark shadowy figures being led away, the throne glowing with righteousness, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great men:
verses.little_bible: Do not push yourself forward in front of important people. Do not stand in the place meant for great people.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not push yourself forward before great people.
verses.meaning: Presuming a place of honour you were not invited to is a form of pride. The wise person does not assume they deserve prominence — they wait to be called forward. This principle echoes Jesus's teaching in Luke 14:7–11.
verses.prayer: God, help me be humble and not push for places of honour.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to push yourself forward too much? Why is that not wise?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children the balance between healthy confidence and the humility of not presuming honour they haven't been given?
verses.do_it_today: When you are in a group today, practise waiting rather than pushing forward. Let others go first.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child waiting patiently at the back of a line near a great door, others moving around them, dignity and calm in the child's posture, watercolour style

verses.kjv: For better it is that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
verses.little_bible: It is better to be invited up than to be sent down. Wait humbly, and someone may call you forward. Push ahead, and you may be asked to step back.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wait to be invited up. Do not rush in.
verses.meaning: The shame of being publicly moved to a lower position is worse than the quiet patience of waiting. This is the wisdom of humility — not in being a doormat, but in not presuming a place that was not yours to take.
verses.prayer: God, help me wait humbly and trust You to lift me up.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever seen someone embarrassed by pushing too far forward? What happened?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children learn to wait to be called forward — in conversation, in achievements, in social situations — rather than always promoting themselves?
verses.do_it_today: Today, let someone else take the place of honour in something. See how it feels to give way graciously.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child waiting quietly at a humble seat, then being warmly invited to come up to a place of honour by a kind host, two panel watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
verses.little_bible: Do not rush into a fight or an argument. If you do not think it through, you may not know what to do when it goes badly. You could end up embarrassed.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not rush into arguments or fights.
verses.meaning: Hasty conflict is unwise because we rarely think through where it will lead. The verse warns against impulsive confrontation — thinking before acting is crucial, especially in disputes.
verses.prayer: God, help me think before I argue or fight with anyone.
verses.discussion_question: What can go wrong when you rush into a fight without thinking?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to pause before entering conflict — to think through whether a dispute is worth it and what the likely outcome is?
verses.do_it_today: The next time something makes you want to argue or fight, stop and count to ten. Think first. Then decide.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child rushing toward a confrontation, then stopping and pulling back to think, a question mark glowing above their head, calm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret of another:
verses.little_bible: If you have a problem with someone, talk to them directly. Do not share their secrets with others to win the argument.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Settle disputes privately. Never share secrets to win.
verses.meaning: The wise course in conflict is direct, private dialogue — not gossip, not dragging in others, not weaponising private knowledge. Sharing someone's secret to gain an advantage is a serious breach of trust.
verses.prayer: God, help me settle problems privately and never use secrets as weapons.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it wrong to share someone's private secret to win an argument?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a culture of direct, private conflict resolution in our family — where grievances are addressed person-to-person, not through third parties?
verses.do_it_today: If you have an unresolved issue with someone, go to them directly today. Do not talk about it with others first.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two children talking privately and honestly face to face, solving a problem together, warm calm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Lest he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
verses.little_bible: If you betray a secret, people who hear about it will think badly of you. That bad reputation may never go away.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Betraying secrets ruins your reputation.
verses.meaning: The consequence of leaking a secret is not just relational damage — it is reputational. A person known as one who betrays confidence carries that mark for a long time. Trust, once broken, is hard to restore.
verses.prayer: God, help me be trustworthy with what people share with me.
verses.discussion_question: What does it feel like when someone shares your secret? Why does it hurt?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to handle confidences wisely — understanding that trustworthiness is built over many small moments of faithfulness?
verses.do_it_today: Is there a secret someone has trusted you with? Guard it today. Tell no one. Build trust.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding a glowing secret gently in closed hands, choosing carefully to protect it, warm and trustworthy watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
verses.little_bible: The right word said at the right time is precious. It is like golden apples in a beautiful silver frame.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The right word at the right time is golden.
verses.meaning: This is one of the most beautiful images in all of Proverbs. Timing and content must meet together for speech to have its full impact. A word that is 'fitly spoken' — timely, true, and fitting — is extraordinarily valuable and beautiful. This is the standard for all wise speech.
verses.prayer: God, help me say the right thing at the right time.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a time someone said exactly the right thing? How did it feel?
verses.family_discussion: How do we practise the art of timely speech in our family — knowing when to speak, how to speak, and what to say — rather than speaking impulsively?
verses.do_it_today: Before you speak in an important moment today, pause and ask: 'Is this the right word? Is this the right time?' Then speak.
verses.illustration_prompt: Golden apples arranged in a beautiful silver frame, glowing with warmth and beauty, one small child pointing at it in wonder, warm watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
verses.little_bible: A beautiful gold earring is lovely on the ear. In the same way, a wise person's correction is precious — when the listener is willing to hear it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise correction received well is like gold.
verses.meaning: Correction has two parts: the one who reproves wisely, and the ear that receives it obediently. Both are required for the proverb to work. A wise word of correction that lands on a willing, humble heart is as beautiful and valuable as fine gold jewellery.
verses.prayer: God, give me an ear that gladly receives wise correction.
verses.discussion_question: When someone corrects you kindly, what is the wise way to respond?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create a family culture where correction is received as a gift rather than resisted as an attack — and where those who give correction do so wisely?
verses.do_it_today: Think of someone who has corrected you recently. Did you receive it like gold? Thank them today if you can.
verses.illustration_prompt: A golden earring glowing on a child's ear, warmth and beauty, a gentle correction being received with a smile, soft watercolour scene

verses.kjv: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
verses.little_bible: Cool snow during harvest time is refreshing and welcome. In the same way, a faithful messenger refreshes the soul of the people who sent them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A faithful messenger refreshes like cool snow.
verses.meaning: Cold snow at harvest time would have been extraordinarily refreshing in the heat of ancient Near Eastern summers. The faithful messenger — who delivers the message accurately and on time — provides that same relief and refreshment to those who depend on them.
verses.prayer: God, help me be faithful and reliable in everything I am sent to do.
verses.discussion_question: What makes a messenger truly faithful? What would happen if they changed the message?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate reliability and faithfulness in our children — the character of someone who can be trusted to carry out a task exactly as given?
verses.do_it_today: When someone gives you a message or task today, carry it out faithfully — exactly as asked, not your own version.
verses.illustration_prompt: A messenger arriving with cool refreshing news, masters lighting up with relief and joy, cool snowflakes and harvest warmth together, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift is like clouds and wind without rain.
verses.little_bible: A person who brags about a gift they never actually give is like clouds and wind with no rain. They promise much but bring nothing.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Empty promises are like clouds with no rain.
verses.meaning: Clouds and wind naturally promise rain — but when they produce nothing, the disappointment is acute, especially in an agricultural society depending on rain. The person who boasts of giving what they never give produces the same bitter disappointment in those who trusted them.
verses.memory_phrase: Keep your promises. Do not boast.
verses.prayer: God, help me only promise what I will truly give.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever been promised something that never came? How did it feel?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model and teach promise-keeping in our family — the integrity of only committing to what we will actually do?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one promise you have made. Are you keeping it? Follow through on it today.
verses.illustration_prompt: Dark clouds building with wind over a dry parched field — no rain falling — a disappointed farmer looking up, gentle but honest watercolour scene

verses.kjv: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
verses.little_bible: Patient waiting and gentle words can change even a ruler's mind. A soft and kind answer can break through the hardest resistance.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Patience and gentle words are very powerful.
verses.meaning: This is one of Proverbs' most striking paradoxes: softness breaks bone. Patience persuades power. The most forceful approach to persuasion is not aggression or pressure, but calm, persistent, gentle speech. This wisdom applies in every relationship.
verses.prayer: God, teach me to speak gently and wait patiently.
verses.discussion_question: When gentle words work better than loud ones, what does that tell us about real strength?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model gentle persuasion over force in our family — showing children that real influence comes through patient, kind speech rather than aggression?
verses.do_it_today: In a difficult conversation today, choose the soft, gentle word over the forceful one. See what happens.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small gentle stream of water slowly wearing through a large rock, soft and patient, the stone gently yielding, beautiful watercolour metaphor

verses.kjv: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
verses.little_bible: If you find honey, eat enough — but not too much. Too much honey will make you sick. Good things become bad when we take too much of them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Too much of a good thing makes you sick.
verses.meaning: Honey is sweet and good, but overindulgence turns it into something harmful. This is a universal wisdom principle: even genuinely good things must be taken in appropriate measure. Excess corrupts the good. This applies to food, pleasure, wealth, and every appetite.
verses.prayer: God, help me enjoy good things without taking too much.
verses.discussion_question: Can you think of a good thing that becomes bad if you have too much of it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate healthy contentment and self-restraint in our children — the wisdom to enjoy good things without overindulging in them?
verses.do_it_today: At mealtime today, practise stopping before you are too full. Notice what 'enough' feels like.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child eating honey with delight then pausing, looking a little unwell from too much — a gentle warning in a warm honey-toned watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and so hate thee.
verses.little_bible: Do not visit your neighbour's house too often. If you are always there, they may grow tired of you and stop enjoying your visits.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Visit friends wisely. Do not overstay.
verses.meaning: Even good friendships can be worn thin by overexposure. Wisdom in relationships includes knowing when to come and when to stay away. The person who values a friendship protects it by not being a burden through constant presence.
verses.prayer: God, help me be a friend who is welcome, not a burden.
verses.discussion_question: How can you show a friend you value them by giving them space sometimes?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children healthy relational rhythms — closeness and space, visiting and staying home — as expressions of wisdom and love?
verses.do_it_today: Think about your closest friend. Are you the right amount of present in their life — not too much, not too little?
verses.illustration_prompt: A child waving goodbye at a neighbour's door, both smiling — space and warmth coexisting, a healthy friendship preserved, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
verses.little_bible: A person who lies about their neighbour is like a heavy hammer, a sharp sword, and a shooting arrow. False words hurt like real weapons.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Lying about others is like hitting them with weapons.
verses.meaning: The three weapons — maul (a heavy club), sword, and arrow — represent different kinds of violent force. Bearing false witness inflicts real damage on real people. This is not merely wrong — it is violent. God takes it with the same seriousness.
verses.prayer: God, keep my mouth from ever lying about anyone.
verses.discussion_question: How can a lie about someone hurt them as much as hitting them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand the weight of bearing false witness — that lying about others is an act of violence, not merely an error?
verses.do_it_today: Think about your words about others today. Have they been completely honest? Commit to speaking only the truth about people.
verses.illustration_prompt: False words flying from a mouth like arrows and swords toward a hurt and grieving figure, the wounds of false witness visible, honest and sober watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
verses.little_bible: Trusting someone who will let you down when you need help is like biting with a broken tooth. It hurts and does not work. It is like a foot that is out of place.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Trusting an unfaithful person in trouble is painful.
verses.meaning: Two vivid physical images: a broken tooth that fails when you need to bite, a dislocated foot that fails when you need to walk. Both are painful and useless at the moment of greatest need. The unfaithful person is exactly like this — worst when needed most.
verses.prayer: God, help me be the kind of friend who never lets people down.
verses.discussion_question: What makes someone truly trustworthy to have around in hard times?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate faithfulness in our children — the deep character quality of being reliable not just when it is easy, but especially when it is hard?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a friend or family member going through a hard time. Be the faithful friend to them today — show up and help.
verses.illustration_prompt: A person reaching for a support that crumbles — like biting with a broken tooth — the pain of misplaced trust vivid in a gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
verses.little_bible: Singing happy songs to someone who is very sad is unkind. It is like taking away their coat in the cold. Read the room — meet people where they are.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not sing happy songs to a sad heart.
verses.meaning: Emotional tone-deafness — being cheerful at the wrong moment — causes real harm. Taking a coat from someone in cold weather and pouring vinegar on soda (nitre) both produce discomfort or violent reaction. Mismatched emotional responses do the same. True compassion requires attentiveness to where people actually are.
verses.prayer: God, help me be kind and caring to people who are sad.
verses.discussion_question: How can you tell when someone needs quiet kindness rather than cheerfulness?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children emotional attentiveness — the wisdom of reading others' emotional states and responding appropriately rather than just expressing their own feelings?
verses.do_it_today: If someone around you seems sad today, ask them quietly how they are. Do not try to cheer them up straight away — just listen.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child gently sitting beside a sad friend in quiet, caring presence — not singing or dancing, just being there — warm and tender watercolour scene

verses.kjv: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
verses.little_bible: If your enemy is hungry, give them food. If they are thirsty, give them water. This is what God asks of you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Feed and care for your enemy.
verses.meaning: This is radical counter-cultural love. The natural instinct is to withhold from an enemy. But God commands provision and care even for those who have wronged us. This prepares the ground for Jesus's command in Matthew 5:44 to love our enemies.
verses.prayer: God, help me be kind even to people who are unkind to me.
verses.discussion_question: Why do you think God asks us to be kind to people who are not kind to us?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that loving enemies is not weakness — it is the highest expression of God's kind of strength, trust, and love?
verses.do_it_today: Think of someone who has been unkind to you. Do one small act of kindness toward them today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child offering a piece of bread and a cup of water to another child who had been unkind, both looking surprised, gentle light of grace in the scene, watercolour style

verses.kjv: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
verses.little_bible: Your kindness to an enemy is like heaping coals of fire on their head — it may awaken their conscience. And God will reward you for your goodness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Kindness to enemies is rewarded by God.
verses.meaning: The 'coals of fire' is a picture of conviction — the discomfort of unearned kindness that awakens a person's conscience to their own wrong. But the verse also gives a clear motivation: God Himself rewards acts of love toward enemies. Justice is not our job — God handles it.
verses.prayer: God, help me trust You to reward me for doing right.
verses.discussion_question: Why can you trust God to take care of things when you choose to be kind instead of getting back?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to leave room for God's justice rather than taking personal revenge — trusting that God sees and rewards their goodness?
verses.do_it_today: In any moment today where you want to 'get back' at someone, choose kindness instead and trust God to handle the rest.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child choosing kindness while a soft divine light watches approvingly from above, the enemy visibly moved, grace and justice together in a warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The north wind driveth away rain: so doth an angry countenance a backbiting tongue.
verses.little_bible: The north wind pushes away rain clouds. In the same way, an angry face can stop a person who likes to say mean things behind other people's backs.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A firm look stops a gossiping tongue.
verses.meaning: Backbiting — speaking ill of others behind their back — is silenced by the clear displeasure of those who refuse to tolerate it. This is a practical wisdom: righteous disapproval of gossip creates the social environment in which gossip cannot thrive.
verses.memory_phrase: Reject gossip with a firm look.
verses.prayer: God, help me never speak badly about others behind their backs.
verses.discussion_question: What should you do when someone starts saying mean things about a person who is not there?
verses.family_discussion: How do we establish a family culture where backbiting and gossip are clearly unwelcome — not through harshness, but through consistent, calm disapproval?
verses.do_it_today: If someone starts gossiping around you today, quietly change the subject or say something kind about the person being talked about.
verses.illustration_prompt: Wind blowing away dark gossip clouds, a child's calm firm expression silencing unkind words, strong and gentle at once, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
verses.little_bible: It is better to live in a small corner of a rooftop than in a big house full of arguing and fighting. Peace is worth more than space.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A small peaceful corner beats a big fighting house.
verses.meaning: This proverb appears also in Proverbs 21:9. Peace in relationships is more valuable than the physical comforts of a large home. Constant conflict makes even a beautiful house unbearable. Harmony is a gift beyond material wealth.
verses.memory_phrase: Peace beats a big fighting house.
verses.prayer: God, help our home be full of peace and kindness.
verses.discussion_question: Why is a peaceful home more important than a big or fancy home?
verses.family_discussion: How do we actively cultivate peace in our home — not just the absence of fighting, but the presence of warmth, kindness, and genuine harmony?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today to make your home more peaceful — a kind word, a resolved conflict, or choosing not to start a fight.
verses.illustration_prompt: A tiny peaceful corner on a rooftop with one content person contrasted with a large house full of chaos and noise, the small corner clearly better, warm watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
verses.little_bible: Good news from far away is like cold water to a very thirsty person. It refreshes and revives the soul that has been waiting and longing.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Good news refreshes like cold water.
verses.meaning: The image is of deep, soul-level refreshment. Good news — especially from afar where no news had come — provides genuine relief and joy. This is why the Gospel, good news from God, is so named: it is exactly this refreshment, arriving at the deepest point of human thirst.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for the good news of Your love and grace.
verses.discussion_question: What is some good news that made you feel truly refreshed and happy inside?
verses.family_discussion: How do we regularly bring truly good news into our family's life — from Scripture, from God's faithfulness, and from stories of His grace in the world?
verses.do_it_today: Share one piece of genuinely good news with your family today. Let it refresh everyone.
verses.illustration_prompt: A thirsty child receiving cold refreshing water from a cup, relief and joy visible on their face — a letter with good news glowing beside them, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A righteous man falling down before the wicked is as a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
verses.little_bible: When a righteous person gives in to wicked people, it is like a fresh spring becoming muddy and corrupt. The good thing becomes spoiled.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A righteous person falling to wickedness corrupts everything.
verses.meaning: A righteous person who compromises or falls to wicked pressure does not just harm themselves — they corrupt a source that others were depending on. A 'troubled fountain' and 'corrupt spring' are both images of something that should refresh but now harms. Our righteousness is not merely personal — others depend on it.
verses.memory_phrase: Stand firm. Do not give way.
verses.prayer: God, help me stand firm and not give in to doing wrong.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it matter when a good and righteous person gives in and does wrong?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that their character is not just personal — it affects others, and standing firm in righteousness is a gift to those around them?
verses.do_it_today: Is there a situation where you have been tempted to give in to something wrong? Stand firm today. Pray for strength.
verses.illustration_prompt: A once-clear spring becoming murky and clouded as a righteous figure stumbles before dark shadows, the water losing its purity, honest and sober watercolour scene

verses.kjv: It is not good to eat much honey: so for men to search their own glory is not glory.
verses.little_bible: Eating too much honey is not good for you. In the same way, always seeking your own praise and glory does not bring real honour.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Seeking your own glory is not true glory.
verses.meaning: Self-promotion is the spiritual equivalent of gorging on honey — it may seem pleasant but it produces something harmful. True glory, in God's economy, is received rather than seized. The one who constantly pushes their own reputation ultimately diminishes it.
verses.prayer: God, help me seek Your glory, not my own.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between being proud of good work and always pushing for your own glory?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children pursue excellence and godly achievement without the self-promoting spirit that ultimately undermines true honour?
verses.do_it_today: Do something good today without telling anyone about it. Let it be between you and God.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child quietly doing a good deed and stepping back, no spotlight sought, warm and humble, the quiet beauty of unsought honour in a gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.
verses.little_bible: A person who cannot control their own feelings and actions is like a city with broken walls and no protection. They are open to every danger.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: No self-control leaves you open to every danger.
verses.meaning: In the ancient world, a city without walls was completely vulnerable — open to any attack, without defence or security. This is the picture of a person with no self-control: every temptation, every enemy, every destructive force finds an open door. Self-control is not merely a virtue — it is structural protection.
verses.prayer: God, help me control myself so I stay safe and strong.
verses.discussion_question: What happens to a city with no walls? What happens to a person who cannot control themselves?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children build the walls of self-control — over anger, appetite, speech, and impulse — as one of the most important and practical expressions of wisdom?
verses.do_it_today: Pick one area where your self-control is weak. Ask God for help with it today. Practice saying no to it once.
verses.illustration_prompt: A crumbling city with broken walls, wide open and exposed to the outside, compared to a strong walled city glowing with protection, child standing inside the protected one, watercolour illustration
